title: Real lab: edit a file in vim
instruction: Real Linux box with real vim. Open /root/notes.txt in vim, add a new line containing the word DONE, then save and quit. Click Verify once you're back at the shell prompt. (vim basics: press i to start typing, Esc to stop, then type :wq and Enter to save and quit.)
setup:
printf 'my notes
- buy milk
- learn vim
' > /root/notes.txt; echo '(scenario ready: /root/notes.txt created)'

verify.command: if grep -q DONE /root/notes.txt 2>/dev/null; then echo VIM_OK; else echo VIM_NO; fi
verify.success: Solved! You opened, edited, and saved a real file in vim. i → type → Esc → :wq is the loop that gets you out of (and productive in) vim.
verify.fail: Not yet, /root/notes.txt needs a saved line containing DONE. In vim: press i, type DONE, press Esc, type :wq and Enter.

hint: vim /root/notes.txt → i → type DONE → Esc → :wq → Enter
